source: Generated in-app placeholder shapes (no photographs) — see Part 20 of the master plan.
reviewer: not yet reviewed by a clinician or cultural advisor — placeholder only
licence: n/a — original vector shapes drawn for this project, no third-party assets
note: These are deliberately generic icon+label items, not photographs of real NER household objects. Several icons (japi, diya, mora, and this expansion pass's ghoti/pankha) are drawn as common everyday NER-regional shapes rather than sterile international clip-art, but they are still original line art, not photographs — the household is still prompted to replace each one with their own photographed object, never presented as 'what NER people recognise'. A real deployment needs an actual reviewed regional photo/sound library sourced with proper provenance and licensing, which this hackathon build does not have access to. Expanded from 6 to 16 objects and 1 to 3 routines (SIH26003 rebuild pass) specifically so Familiar Pairs / Sound & Sight / My Next Step don't show the identical fixed set every single session before any family content exists — this is a content-authoring fix, not a game-logic change.

sounds.note: Part 20 names timbrally distinct sounds (temple_bell.wav, wooden_clapper.wav, bamboo_flute.wav, rain_on_tin_roof.wav, morning_birds.wav) as the intended fallback library. No licensed audio was available to record or source for this build, and we will not ship synthesized sine-tone substitutes — the plan explicitly warns those are indistinguishable on cheap tablet speakers for presbycusis, which would make the fallback actively worse than no fallback. Sound & Sight therefore degrades to visual-only matching when no family-recorded pack audio exists, with an honest on-screen note, instead of a fake sound.
